patterns.title: Event Streaming
patterns.summary: Move business events through Oracle AI Database with transactional queues, JMS, OKafka, and durable consumers.
patterns.useWhen: Use this when the event and the data change need the same transactional boundary, or when a team wants streaming without standing up a separate broker first.

patterns.title: Kafka Migration
patterns.summary: Move Kafka-style producers and consumers toward Oracle AI Database queues while preserving event payload and processing shape.
patterns.useWhen: Use this for staged migration, Kafka API interoperability, or comparing separate-broker designs with database-native eventing.

patterns.title: Semantic Search / RAG
patterns.summary: Combine embeddings, text filters, and SQL access paths for retrieval-augmented application features.
patterns.useWhen: Use this when users search by meaning, when an AI answer needs grounded records, or when vector and keyword relevance both matter.

patterns.title: AI Agents
patterns.summary: Give agents durable memory, SQL tools, and MCP-backed access to Oracle AI Database workflows.
patterns.useWhen: Use this when the application needs tool calling, persistent memory, or natural-language access to database-backed operations.

patterns.title: JSON Documents and Duality
patterns.summary: Model flexible JSON documents, stream OSON payloads, run SQL/JSON analytics, and expose relational models through JSON Relational Duality Views.
patterns.useWhen: Use this when records need document flexibility, document-shaped APIs, or JSON views over relational data without giving up indexes, SQL, constraints, and transactions.

patterns.title: API Facades
patterns.summary: Expose Oracle AI Database through REST, MongoDB-compatible, and GraphQL-style interfaces.
patterns.useWhen: Use this when clients should not own low-level SQL details, or when an existing app expects REST, MongoDB, or GraphQL-style access.

patterns.title: Graph Modeling
patterns.summary: Represent connected data as property graphs or GraphQL-style query shapes over Oracle AI Database tables.
patterns.useWhen: Use this when relationships are first-class: recommendations, networks, paths, impact analysis, lineage, or traversal-heavy screens.

patterns.title: Spatial Querying
patterns.summary: Store, index, and query location-aware data with spatial operators and geometry types.
patterns.useWhen: Use this when the product asks questions about proximity, containment, routing, zones, or other location-aware behavior.

patterns.title: Local Testing
patterns.summary: Run deterministic integration tests against disposable Oracle AI Database Free containers.
patterns.useWhen: Use this when tests need real database behavior without sharing a long-lived development instance.

patterns.title: Application Foundations
patterns.summary: Connect applications to Oracle AI Database with drivers, local sandboxes, and transaction workflows.
patterns.useWhen: Use this when the work is setting up application access, local tool environments, or transaction behavior before higher-level feature work.

patterns.title: Database Security
patterns.summary: Keep application data access decisions close to Oracle AI Database with identity-aware guardrails and auditable authorization paths.
patterns.useWhen: Use this when one application account needs different row, column, write, or audit outcomes for different end users or service flows.

patterns.title: Spring Boot
patterns.summary: Use Oracle AI Database with Spring Boot for persistence, resource loading, isolated service data, configuration, dynamic properties, and secrets-aware setup.
patterns.useWhen: Use this when Spring Boot services need database-backed persistence, resource loading, clean service boundaries, runtime configuration, or environment-specific wiring.

patterns.title: Observability
patterns.summary: Correlate database work with application traces, client metadata, and messaging flows.
patterns.useWhen: Use this when teams need to follow a request from HTTP or JMS through JDBC calls and into Oracle AI Database sessions.
